title.narrative: JOUD: Netherlands-Jordan Upscaling and Development of Competitiveness in the Food Processing Sector

description.narrative: JOUD is a private sector development initiative that aims to strengthen the competitiveness of Jordan's food processing sector by improving enterprise performance, addressing market system constraints, and creating sustainable trade and investment linkages with the Netherlands and Europe. The project builds on the experience and lessons learned from the previously implemented Netherlands-funded Corporate Entrepreneurship Responsibility Alliance (CERA) project, while introducing a more systemic and market-oriented approach focused on long-term competitiveness and commercial sustainability. The project contributes to sustainable economic growth and decent job creation by supporting food processing MSMEs to become more productive, resource-efficient, export-ready, and commercially competitive. It adopts a Market Systems Development (MSD) approach, recognising that sustainable sector transformation requires addressing both firm-level constraints and wider market bottlenecks. The project is structured around three mutually reinforcing results. First, it supports enterprise upgrading through comprehensive competitiveness diagnostics, tailored technical assistance, business advisory services, and co-investment grants that enable enterprises to improve productivity, quality compliance, digital readiness, occupational health and safety, and water and energy efficiency. Second, JOUD addresses structural logistics and cold-chain constraints affecting the food processing sector by undertaking market system diagnostics, developing investment-ready business cases, and facilitating a Netherlands–Jordan logistics partnership that mobilises Dutch expertise and encourages future investments. Rather than financing infrastructure directly, the project plays a catalytic role by identifying, structuring, and de-risking investment opportunities for financial institutions, development partners, and private investors. Third, the project strengthens commercial linkages between Jordanian enterprises and Dutch and European markets through export readiness support, targeted market intelligence, buyer engagement, and the establishment of the Dutch Export Academy – Jordan. The project adopts a demand-driven and adaptive implementation approach. Enterprise support is based on structured diagnostics and tailored competitiveness roadmaps, ensuring that interventions respond to the specific needs of participating enterprises. Cross-cutting priorities—including women's economic participation, youth employment, environmental sustainability, water productivity, digitalisation, and decent work—are integrated throughout the project design and beneficiary selection process. Implementation will be led by Leaders International in partnership with specialised Dutch and Jordanian technical and knowledge partners, while working in close coordination with relevant public institutions and complementary donor programmes. The project also seeks to institutionalise key methodologies, knowledge products, and export promotion approaches to ensure sustainability beyond the implementation period and contribute to the long-term competitiveness of Jordan's food processing sector.
